# A component built at run time gives back what it kept when it is
# destroyed, on each platform placement writes C for: its record's destroy
# drops each field it kept -- a string, a list and its elements -- and then
# the record, a box kept like any other block (ir.Func.Frees). It gave back
# nothing, so each row a rebuilt list made grew the runtime's kept set by
# its prop, its vars and, on win32, the record itself. The test counts the
# kept blocks through the runtime's sngl_kept_blocks. Go collects what it
# allocates, so the program is C's alone.
#
# A row rendering a slot of its own also lets go of the anchor gtk4 keeps
# for it (#[gen.protocol(anchor)]): its teardown asks gtk4.sngl's _slotAnchor with no
# box, which gives back the reference the var held. Each row a rebuilt list
# destroyed kept its hidden label alive. anchor.sngl counts the labels GTK
# has not finalized, through a gtk_label_new of count.c's that the runtime's
# calls resolve to.

# A closure gives back what it captured. Its environment is made in the
# turn's arena behind a header saying how it is kept (sngl_env), a holder
# storing it keeps a counted copy the holders after it share, and the last
# to let go gives it back with the holder's value: a package var's
# replaced, a record's prop box (ir.StructDef.Counted) as the record is
# destroyed, a callback's context as C releases it. Each
# closure.sngl test fails where the environment was a heap copy nothing gave
# back, which kept what it captured.

[!gtk4] skip 'gtk4 needs its development libraries to build'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=c app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=win32 --language=c app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=c anchor.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=c closure.sngl
stdout 'ok +2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=win32 --language=c closure.sngl
stdout 'ok +2 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import c "sngl:x/c"
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

c.link(include="sngl.h")

// How many blocks the runtime keeps: what every holder holds.
#[c.native("sngl_kept_blocks")]
func keptBlocks() int

component row(label string) ui.node {
    var note = "row {label}"
    var tags list[string] = ["a {label}", "b {label}"]

    ui.text(value="{note} {tags.length()}")
}

component rows ui.node {
    var round = 0
    var labels list[string] = ["r0a", "r0b", "r0c"]

    ui.vbox {
        ui.button #next(text="next", @click {
            round += 1
            labels = ["r{round}a", "r{round}b", "r{round}c"]
        })
        for var l = labels {
            row(label=l)
        }
    }
}

func testARebuiltListKeepsNoMore(t test.Test, r rows) {
    r.next.click()
    var before = keptBlocks()
    r.next.click()
    r.next.click()
    t.assert(keptBlocks() == before)
}

ui.window(title="t") {
    rows
}
-- anchor.sngl --
import c "sngl:x/c"
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

c.link(include="count.h", sources=["count.c", "count.h"])

// How many labels GTK has made and not yet finalized (count.c).
#[c.native("labels_alive")]
func labelsAlive() int

component row(label string) ui.node {
    var open = true

    ui.vbox {
        if open {
            ui.text(value="A {label}")
        }
        ui.text(value="B")
    }
}

component rows ui.node {
    var round = 0
    var labels list[string] = ["r0a", "r0b", "r0c"]

    ui.vbox {
        ui.button #next(text="next", @click {
            round += 1
            labels = ["r{round}a", "r{round}b", "r{round}c"]
        })
        for var l = labels {
            row(label=l)
        }
    }
}

func testARebuiltListKeepsNoMoreLabels(t test.Test, r rows) {
    r.next.click()
    var before = labelsAlive()
    r.next.click()
    r.next.click()
    var after = labelsAlive()
    t.assert(before > 0)
    t.assert(after == before)
}

ui.window(title="t") {
    rows
}
-- count.h --
#include <stdint.h>

/* labels_alive is how many labels GTK has made and not yet finalized, once
 * the main loop has nothing waiting. */
int64_t labels_alive(void);
-- count.c --
#define _GNU_SOURCE
#include <dlfcn.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <gtk/gtk.h>
#include "count.h"

static int64_t alive;

static void gone(gpointer data, GObject *w) {
    alive--;
}

/* The program's gtk_label_new is the one the runtime's calls resolve to: it
 * makes the label GTK's does and counts it until it is finalized. */
GtkWidget *gtk_label_new(const char *s) {
    static GtkWidget *(*real)(const char *);
    if (real == NULL) {
        void *p = dlsym(RTLD_NEXT, "gtk_label_new");
        memcpy(&real, &p, sizeof p);
    }
    GtkWidget *w = real(s);
    alive++;
    g_object_weak_ref(G_OBJECT(w), gone, NULL);
    return w;
}

int64_t labels_alive(void) {
    while (g_main_context_iteration(NULL, FALSE)) {
    }
    return alive;
}
-- closure.sngl --
import c "sngl:x/c"
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

c.link(include="sngl.h")

// How many blocks the runtime keeps: what every holder holds.
#[c.native("sngl_kept_blocks")]
func keptBlocks() int

var said = ""
var greet = func() {}

func setGreeting(name string) {
    greet = func() {
        said = "hello {name}"
    }
}

component rows ui.node {
    var round = 0
    var labels list[string] = ["r0a", "r0b", "r0c"]
    var picked = ""

    ui.vbox {
        ui.button #next(text="next", @click {
            round += 1
            labels = ["r{round}a", "r{round}b", "r{round}c"]
        })
        for var l = labels {
            ui.button(text=l, @click {
                picked = "{l} picked"
            })
        }
    }
}

func testARebuiltListsHandlersKeepNoMore(t test.Test, r rows) {
    r.next.click()
    var before = keptBlocks()
    r.next.click()
    r.next.click()
    t.assert(keptBlocks() == before)
}

func testAReplacedClosureGivesBackWhatItCaptured(t test.Test, r rows) {
    setGreeting("a{r.round}")
    var before = keptBlocks()
    setGreeting("b{r.round}")
    setGreeting("c{r.round}")
    t.assert(keptBlocks() == before)
    greet()
    t.assert(said == "hello c0")
}

ui.window(title="t") {
    rows
}
